answers.answer: Shuffle the asset, demand, event, investment, and five separate action-type decks; put events in their box and the others by their matching slots. Draw one shuffled setup card, place each listed component in each listed district, and put the specified number of top assets face down on turn slots from slot 1; return setup cards. Round starts at 1, each resource at 0, reveal the top demand and set targets to its printed values. Players choose corporations and take matching sheets and faceup emergencies; use the four-player side at four, otherwise five/six side (Melange unchanged). Randomly choose the first player; threat starts at 0, first player has 10 capital and clockwise players 11, 12, etc. Deal one participating-corporation-or-Federalist rival facedown to each player; put the extra under the board and return unused corporation rivals. Each draws two investments, keeps one facedown, and returns the other facedown to the deck top. Complete setup applies, not the simplified first-game setup.

evidence.section: Overview
evidence.text: This summary covers the complete base game and normal complete setup. The Learn to Play's simplified first-game setup and preset hands are excluded.

evidence.section: Setup, steps 1–9
evidence.text:
1. Decks: Shuffle assets, demands, events and investments separately. Place events in their board box and the other decks beside their matching slots. Separate actions into their five types and shuffle each into its own deck beside its matching slot.
2. City and turn track: Shuffle setup cards and draw one. For every component listed, place one copy in each listed district. Take the number of assets printed in the setup card's upper-right corner from the asset deck and place them facedown, one per turn-track slot, starting at slot 1. Return all setup cards to the box. Unrest/outage go in condition boxes, illness/development in their matching frames, units on district art.
3. Tracks: Put the round marker at 1 and each resource at 0. Reveal the top demand. Set each target token to the printed amount on its resource track.
4. Corporations: Each player chooses a corporation, taking its sheet and matching emergency action faceup. Use the side marked with the four-player icon at four players; otherwise use the five/six-player side. Melange is unchanged between sizes.
5. First player and capital: Randomly select one participating capital token. That corporation takes the active-player token. Set threat to 0. The active player starts at 10 capital; proceeding clockwise, the others start at 11, 12, 13, and so on.
6. Hands: Each player draws the number/types on their sheet, using its printed top-to-bottom order and the General rule below.
7. Rivals: Shuffle the participating corporations' rival cards together with the Federalist. Deal one facedown to each player; place the extra facedown and partly under the board. Secretly inspect your own rival without revealing or discussing it. Return unused corporations' rival cards to the box.
8. Investments: Each player draws two investments, keeps one facedown in their play area, and returns the other facedown to the top of the investment deck. Do not reveal the rejected card.
9. Reserve: Sort unused android, outage, unrest, illness and development tokens and Human First, orgcrime and prisec units into piles beside the board.

clauses: draws for each corporation at four players
answers.answer: Four players: Globalsec 2 security then 1 General; Haas-Bioroid 2 labor then 1 General; Jinteki 2 biotech then 1 General; Melange 1 General, 1 General, 1 General; NBN 2 media then 1 General; Weyland 2 construction then 1 General. Five/six: Globalsec 2 security then 1 media; Haas-Bioroid 2 labor then 1 construction; Jinteki 2 biotech then 1 labor; Melange three separate General draws; NBN 2 media then 1 biotech; Weyland 2 construction then 1 security. Follow the listed top-to-bottom order. Each General is a separate choice of an action type not already drawn during that Refresh, chosen before seeing cards; a multi-card General draw uses one chosen type. Melange therefore chooses three different types.

Each General entry is a separate draw: choose one action type not already drawn during this Refresh step, before seeing its cards. A multiple-card General entry would all come from one chosen type. Melange's three separate General entries therefore use three different types.

answers.answer: Resolve start-of-turn assets before Refresh. Refresh readies exhausted assets, then draws the corporation’s listed action cards in order with General restrictions. Resolve one deal. At End of Turn, each End of Turn ability may be used once in chosen order; an asset received with that header during this step may also be used that turn. Discard action cards to at most hand size (normally five); emergencies are outside the hand. Pass the active token left. The Action Phase ends after a turn if no assets remain on the turn track; otherwise the next active player acts. Not every player is guaranteed a turn in a round.

evidence.section: Standard round and active turn, full procedure
evidence.text:
During the Action Phase, the active player takes one turn:

1. Resolve assets that trigger **at the start of your turn**, before Refresh.
2. **Refresh:** Ready all your exhausted assets, then draw your sheet's action cards in printed top-to-bottom order. Apply the General restrictions above.
3. **Resolve one deal**, as described under Actions.
4. **End of Turn:** You may use each of your End of Turn asset abilities once, in your chosen order. If you receive another asset with that header during this step, you may use its ability this turn too. Then discard action cards until your hand is no larger than your hand size (normally five). Emergencies are outside the hand and do not count. Pass the active-player token left.

If no assets remain on the turn track at the end of the turn, the Action Phase ends. Otherwise, the new active player takes another turn. The last deal still has its full end-of-turn step before Production begins.

evidence.section: Standard round and active turn, turn count
evidence.text: The setup card sets the first Action Phase's turn count; subsequent events set later turn counts. Some players may get no turn in a particular round.

clauses: order of effect, claim and cleanup
answers.answer: Steps: (1) reveal the rightmost remaining turn-track asset (highest occupied slot); (2) active player must place one hand action or faceup emergency in Main Offer and cannot pass; (3) eligible opponents get one chance each to pass or counter; (4) if a counteroffer exists, eligible players get one support chance each; (5) compare support-card counts, resolve the winning offer, then claim the revealed asset. Cleanup discards all played ordinary actions facedown and returns proposed emergencies to their original corporation, facedown if won and faceup otherwise.

evidence.section: Resolving a deal, complete five-step procedure
evidence.text:
There are five steps. Cards offered and cards supporting an offer have different roles. Only the winning offer's instructions resolve; support cards count as cards, regardless of their text/type.

1. **Asset:** Reveal the rightmost remaining asset on the turn track (highest-numbered occupied slot), read it aloud and put it in Revealed Asset.
2. **Main Offer:** The active player must place one action from hand or a faceup emergency faceup in Main Offer. They cannot pass.
3. **Counteroffer:** Starting left of the active player, each other player gets exactly one clockwise chance to pass or propose one hand action or faceup emergency faceup in Counteroffer.
4. **Support:** With no counteroffer, skip this step. Otherwise, everyone except the active player and current countering player is a supporting player, including a displaced earlier counterer. Starting with the first supporter left of the active player, each gets exactly one clockwise chance to support or abstain. Support uses one or more hand actions facedown beside either offer. A player cannot support both offers or get a later second opportunity to add cards. Active/countering players cannot support without explicit ability permission. Emergencies cannot support.
5. **Resolution:** The offer with more facedown support cards wins. A tie, including 0–0, goes to the active player's main offer. The winner resolves their offer and **then** claims the revealed asset faceup in their play area. All played ordinary actions, including superseded/losing offers and support, go facedown to the shared discard. Return every proposed emergency to its original logo corporation: face down if it won, face up otherwise.

answers.answer: The first counteroffer costs 0 additional hand-card discards, the second costs 1, and the third costs 2 (each discard is in addition to playing the offered action). The active player cannot counter absent an explicit ability. Each opponent has exactly one chance; no second circuit occurs. An earlier proposer displaced by a later counteroffer is no longer the current countering player and may support, because displaced earlier counterers are eligible supporters.

evidence.section: Resolving a deal, counteroffer and support steps
evidence.text:
3. **Counteroffer:** Starting left of the active player, each other player gets exactly one clockwise chance to pass or propose one hand action or faceup emergency faceup in Counteroffer. Before adding it, discard hand actions equal to the faceup cards already in that box: first counteroffer costs 0 additional cards, second 1, third 2, etc. Place the new offer on top. Only the topmost is the current counteroffer; previous offers only affect this escalation cost. Its proposer becomes the countering player, replacing the prior one. Another copy of an already offered action is legal. The active player cannot counter unless an ability explicitly permits it. There is no second circuit around the table.
4. **Support:** With no counteroffer, skip this step. Otherwise, everyone except the active player and current countering player is a supporting player, including a displaced earlier counterer.

answers.answer: With a counteroffer, everyone except the active player and current countering player may support, including displaced earlier counterers. Each supporter gets one clockwise opportunity to commit one or more hand actions facedown beside either one offer; support cards count as cards, regardless of text/type. A player cannot support both offers or add cards later; active/countering players need an explicit ability to support, and emergencies cannot support. Each offer wins by having more facedown support cards; a 2–2 tie goes to the active player’s main offer. If nobody counteroffers, skip Support and the main offer proceeds to resolution.

evidence.section: Resolving a deal, Support and Resolution
evidence.text:
4. **Support:** With no counteroffer, skip this step. Otherwise, everyone except the active player and current countering player is a supporting player, including a displaced earlier counterer. Starting with the first supporter left of the active player, each gets exactly one clockwise chance to support or abstain. Support uses one or more hand actions facedown beside either offer. A player cannot support both offers or get a later second opportunity to add cards. Active/countering players cannot support without explicit ability permission. Emergencies cannot support.
5. **Resolution:** The offer with more facedown support cards wins. A tie, including 0–0, goes to the active player's main offer.

answers.answer: Only a faceup emergency can be offered as main or counteroffer; an emergency cannot support. A winning emergency returns facedown; losing or superseded emergencies return faceup. It always returns to its original corporation, even if stolen and offered by another player. Emergencies are outside the hand, excluded from hand size, and cannot be taken/discarded by ordinary effects targeting hand actions. Bryan Stinson, when claimed and discarded, steals two emergency actions from participating corporations; they may be faceup or facedown and retain their state while stolen. Unused corporations’ emergencies cannot be stolen.

evidence.section: Emergency actions, complete operative paragraph
evidence.text: An emergency is kept outside your hand, faceup initially. Only a faceup emergency may be offered as main offer or counteroffer. Winning uses it: it returns facedown and cannot be offered again unless an effect flips it faceup. Losing or superseded emergencies return faceup. Always return it to the original corporation, even if another player stole and offered it. It cannot be used as support, counted toward hand size, or taken/discarded by an ordinary effect targeting actions in hand.

evidence.section: Assets, claiming, exhaustion and theft, Bryan paragraph
evidence.text: Stealing a hand action keeps it secret from the other players. Ordinary action theft cannot take an emergency. Bryan Stinson's explicit ability, when claimed, discards him to steal 2 emergency actions from participating corporations. Those emergencies may be faceup or facedown and keep their state while stolen; they still return to their original owner on discard, facedown if winning and faceup otherwise. Unused corporations' emergencies cannot be stolen.

answers.answer: It produces 0 credits: development would add 1 to primary credits, but orgcrime suppresses all primary production. It produces 1 entertainment secondary. Since it starts in protest, production occurs first, then ordinary unrest rises to strike. Starting in strike or outage yields no resources; outage treats unrest as stable and unable to increase. Normal Production exploits only android districts, so non-android districts do not produce in that phase.

evidence.section: Production, unrest and outages, production modifier table
evidence.text:
| Condition | Production / exploitation effect |
|---|---|
| Stable or protest | Can produce normally. |
| Strike | Produces no resources. Ordinary unrest increases cannot go beyond strike. |
| Outage | Produces no resources. Treat unrest as stable and unable to increase while the outage remains. |
| Development | Add 1 to the primary quantity only; never changes secondary. |
| Orgcrime | Produces no primary, even if developed. Secondary is still available. A one-resource district with orgcrime produces nothing. |
| Human First | Changes the unrest increase upon exploitation from 1 to 2 stages; does not itself prevent that exploitation's initial production. |

evidence.section: Production, unrest and outages, post-table paragraphs
evidence.text:
Supply tracks cap at their last numbered space, and resources at 0 cannot be reduced further. Production is resolved before exploitation's unrest increase: a district starting in protest can produce and then go on strike. A district with an android is still exploited if strike, outage or orgcrime prevents production.

Unrest progresses **stable → protest → strike**, and decreases in reverse order. Stable has no unrest token; protest uses its protest side; strike its strike side. A decrease from protest to stable removes the token. Stable cannot decrease; strike cannot normally increase. Unrest and development tokens never move along paths.

evidence.section: Production Phase
evidence.text:
Exploit every district containing an android, in ascending district-number order. A district without an android is not exploited in normal Production. Exploiting has two parts in order:

1. Produce its resources, applying the existing production modifiers below and increasing the matching supply tracks.
2. Increase its unrest by one stage, or two if it contains Human First. This still happens when it produced nothing. Apply the special Human First outage rule below.

clauses: Human First from four starting conditions
ordinary failed increase without Human First
answers.answer: From stable, Human First’s two-stage exploitation increase reaches strike. From protest or strike, the increase cannot rise by two, so place an outage; a new outage removes unrest and leaves stable. From already-outage, the newly placed outage must move. Without Human First, an ordinary capped unrest increase does not create an outage.

evidence.section: Production, unrest and outages, Human First paragraph
evidence.text: Human First is a specific exception upon exploitation. From stable, its two-stage increase reaches strike. From protest, strike or outage, unrest cannot increase by two, so place an outage. A newly placed outage removes any unrest token and leaves the district stable; this is **not** an NBN contract decrease. If already in outage, the new outage must move. No other ordinary capped unrest increase creates an outage. Removing an outage leaves stable unrest.

clauses: prisec interaction and route to Root
answers.answer: The incoming orgcrime would duplicate the existing orgcrime, so it moves along the exiting path toward higher-numbered districts. If it reaches a prisec-protected district, prisec forces the enemy unit to move onward; it does not remove it. On reaching the Root, the orgcrime returns to reserve and adds 2 threat. Movement out of a district or return at the Root is not removal, so it triggers no district-removal contract. Androids instead move to any district, ignoring paths, one at a time, and cannot enter a district already containing an android.

evidence.section: Placement, movement and the Root, complete operative paragraphs
evidence.text:
A district can have at most one each of android, development, illness, outage, prisec, Human First and orgcrime. Different types can coexist except that prisec forces enemy units to move. Human First and orgcrime are enemies; prisec is not. Unrest/outage share the condition box, with outage removing unrest.

Placing means taking a component from the reserve. If a newly placed or arriving enemy, illness or outage would duplicate its type in a district, that incoming component moves along the district's exiting arrow toward its higher-numbered destination. Continue through successive destinations until it can stay or reaches the Root. If an enemy is placed/moved into a prisec district, or prisec is placed into a district with enemies, each affected enemy moves; prisec does not remove the enemy. The path exiting Base de Cayambe (10) leads to the Root.

The Root is not a district and not part of the city of ten districts. Each enemy, illness or outage that reaches it returns to reserve and adds 2 threat. Moving out of a district is not removal, and the Root return triggers no removal contract. By contrast, an effect that removes a token/unit from a district returns it to reserve and can satisfy the appropriate action-triggered contract.

Android movement is different: move to any district, ignoring paths. Move several androids one at a time and never into a district already containing an android. This prevents directly swapping two occupied android positions as though movement were simultaneous.

clauses: illness action trigger incl chosen/failed destinations
answers.answer: When an action resolves and involves at least one ill district, it adds 2 threat total. A district is involved if chosen, or if a token/unit is placed there, removed from it, or moved into/out of it; attempted placements/moves count at intended destinations even if blocked by components or shortage. Several ill districts still add only 2 total. Production and events do not trigger the action illness effect. An illness token entering the Root separately returns to reserve and adds 2 threat.

evidence.section: Illness and involved districts, complete subsection
evidence.text:
When an action resolves and involves at least one ill district, add **2 threat total**, regardless of how many ill districts were involved. A district is involved if it is chosen for the action, or a token/unit is placed there, removed from it, or moved into/out of it. An attempted placement/move still involves the intended destination if prevented by other components or component shortage. Actions increasing/decreasing unrest choose districts and can therefore trigger illness. An explicit action exception that illness does not increase threat overrides this effect.

Exploitation and event cards do not trigger illness's action effect. An illness token entering the Root still causes the separate 2-threat Root increase, just like an enemy or outage.

evidence.text: The Root is not a district and not part of the city of ten districts. Each enemy, illness or outage that reaches it returns to reserve and adds 2 threat. Moving out of a district is not removal, and the Root return triggers no removal contract. By contrast, an effect that removes a token/unit from a district returns it to reserve and can satisfy the appropriate action-triggered contract.

Movement out and Root returns are not removals and do not trigger removal contracts.

answers.answer: Players may trade capital, assets, and promises at any time; gifts of capital/assets without return are legal. They cannot freely trade action cards, emergencies, investments, rivals, or corporation sheets. A fully and immediately fulfillable agreed trade is binding. Three-or-more-player trades are binding when all parts can resolve immediately and simultaneously. Future promises are nonbinding; if participants cannot agree beforehand whether a trade is binding, it is nonbinding. An exhausted traded asset remains exhausted and is not readied by transfer.

evidence.section: Negotiation and trading, complete subsection
evidence.text:
Players can trade capital, assets and promises at any time; gifts of capital/assets without return are legal. Players **cannot trade action cards, emergency cards, investments, rivals or corporation sheets** (FAQ-corrected RR65.5). An ability explicitly giving, stealing or swapping a normally untradeable card is distinct from freely trading it.

An agreed trade that all participants can immediately and completely fulfill is binding and must be completed. Trades involving three or more players are binding when every part can resolve immediately and simultaneously. A future promise is nonbinding; either party may renege. If players cannot agree before the trade whether it is binding, it is nonbinding. For example, buying support at the moment that supporter must choose can be binding; buying a promise before that player's support opportunity is nonbinding. Trading an exhausted asset does not ready it, and receiving it does not count as claiming it.

clauses: new End of Turn asset usability
answers.answer: If one player controls several abilities with the same timing, they choose the order; across players, resolve them clockwise from the active player. “May” abilities and End of Turn abilities are optional. Exhausted assets ready at the start of Refresh, after start-of-turn triggers. End of Turn abilities can each be used once during that step; if another asset with that header is received during the step, its ability can also be used that turn.

evidence.section: Assets, claiming, exhaustion and theft, timing paragraph
evidence.text: To exhaust an asset, rotate it 90 degrees clockwise. An exhausted asset cannot be exhausted again. Ready your exhausted assets at the start of Refresh, after any start-of-turn triggers. Exhausted assets stay exhausted when traded or stolen. If you control several abilities with the same timing, choose their order. If multiple players use same-timing assets, resolve them clockwise from the active player. Abilities saying “may” and End of Turn abilities are optional; apply the once-per-ability end-of-turn limit in Turn Structure.

evidence.section: Standard round and active turn, End of Turn step
evidence.text: **End of Turn:** You may use each of your End of Turn asset abilities once, in your chosen order. If you receive another asset with that header during this step, you may use its ability this turn too.

answers.answer: 1) Score investments: reveal each and award printed capital; if a required resource is below target, that investment pays zero. 2) Pay demand: demand succeeds only if every supply meets/exceeds its target; if even one is short, fail and add the demand’s printed failure threat once. 3) Reveal demand: reset all resources to 0 regardless of success/failure, put old demand under deck, reveal next, set targets. 4) Choose investment: return all investments, shuffle, draw two each, keep one facedown and return the other facedown to the top; unchosen cards are not revealed. In the third demand, after Pay Demand the game ends immediately; omit Reveal Demand and Choose Investment.

evidence.section: Demand round, full four-step procedure
evidence.text:
Resolve these steps in order:

1. **Score Investment:** Reveal each player's facedown investment and award its printed capital. If an investment requires a resource to meet demand and that resource is below its target, it yields zero. Apply its printed formula and cap when eligible.
2. **Pay Demand:** If every resource's supply equals or exceeds its target, demand is met and no threat is added. If even one is short, demand fails: increase threat once by the demand card's printed failure amount. Investments were already scored before this check. If this is the third demand round, the game ends immediately after this step; omit steps 3–4. Threat reaching 25 still ends the game immediately and uses the Federalist ending.
3. **Reveal Demand:** Reset every resource to 0, put the old demand under its deck, reveal the new top demand and set each target to the new printed value. This reset happens whether the previous demand succeeded or failed; surplus is not carried over.
4. **Choose Investment:** Return all investments to their deck and shuffle. Each player draws two, keeps one facedown, and returns the other facedown to the top without revealing it. Advance to the next standard round.

evidence.section: Discards, replenishment and information, investment information sentence
evidence.text: Chosen investments remain facedown until demand; unchosen investments are not revealed. Do not inspect the investment deck after cards are dealt.

clauses: Federalist win at 25 capital when threat reaches 25
below-25 third-demand result and named-rival tie
answers.answer: Yes. Investments score before Pay Demand, so the final demand’s investment is scored before its failure raises threat to 25. At threat 25, every ordinary corporation loses; the Federalist wins only if it has at least 25 capital at that moment (otherwise everyone loses). If the third demand finishes below 25, an ordinary player with another corporation as rival wins only by strictly exceeding that rival’s capital; a tie loses. If your rival is your own corporation, you must strictly exceed at least 2 other players in a four-player game, or at least 3 in a five/six-player game; ties do not count as beaten.

evidence.section: Demand round, Score Investment and Pay Demand steps
evidence.text:
1. **Score Investment:** Reveal each player's facedown investment and award its printed capital. If an investment requires a resource to meet demand and that resource is below its target, it yields zero. Apply its printed formula and cap when eligible.
2. **Pay Demand:** If every resource's supply equals or exceeds its target, demand is met and no threat is added. If even one is short, demand fails: increase threat once by the demand card's printed failure amount. Investments were already scored before this check. If this is the third demand round, the game ends immediately after this step; omit steps 3–4. Threat reaching 25 still ends the game immediately and uses the Federalist ending.

evidence.section: Scoring / Victory Conditions, complete result table
evidence.text:
| Ending / rival | Result |
|---|---|
| Third demand finishes with threat below 25; rival names another corporation | Win if your capital is strictly higher than that corporation's. A tie loses. |
| Third demand finishes below 25; rival is your own corporation | Win if you strictly exceed at least 2 other players in a four-player game, or at least 3 in a five/six-player game. Tied players do not count as beaten. |
| Third demand finishes below 25; Federalist | Federalist loses, regardless of capital. |
| Threat reaches 25 at any time, including failure of the final demand | Every ordinary corporation loses. Only the Federalist can win, and only with at least 25 capital at that moment; otherwise everyone loses. |

answers.answer: Players cannot tell others which actions they hold and cannot lie about hand counts. Rivals cannot be revealed or discussed. Chosen investments remain facedown until demand; unchosen investments are not revealed, and players may not inspect the investment deck after dealing. Facedown turn-track assets cannot be inspected. Event fronts seen through a look/reorder ability must remain secret; event backs are public, including the top deck card’s back. Thomas Haas requires openly stating whether you swap the under-board rival with your own; whether a swap happened is public, though rival identities remain secret.

evidence.text: Players cannot tell others which actions are in their hands, and cannot lie about hand counts. Actions stolen or given by an effect remain secret from others. Rivals cannot be revealed or discussed. Do not inspect facedown turn-track assets. Event fronts seen with a look/reorder ability must stay secret; event backs, including the back of the deck's top card, are public.

answers.answer: Ordinary actions go facedown to the shared discard pile, where players cannot inspect them. Discarded assets go facedown to the bottom of the asset deck. Removed components return to the reserve and may be reused. If a needed action type deck is empty, shuffle the entire shared discard, reveal and sort by type, then shuffle each type into its respective deck, replenishing all affected decks. If the reserve lacks a required component, do not place it. Supply tracks cap at their last numbered space, so production cannot carry supply beyond the track end.

evidence.section: Components, component limits paragraph
evidence.text: Components are limited to those supplied. If the reserve has no copy of a required component, do not place it. Removed components return to the reserve and can be reused.

evidence.section: Discards, replenishment and information, complete opening paragraph
evidence.text: All ordinary actions are discarded facedown to the shared discard pile; players cannot look at them as discarded or while in that pile. If a requested action type is empty when drawing, shuffle the entire shared discard, reveal and sort its cards by type, then shuffle each type into its respective deck. This replenishes all affected action decks, not merely the requested type. Assets instead go facedown under their own deck.

evidence.section: Production, unrest and outages, supply cap sentence
evidence.text: Supply tracks cap at their last numbered space, and resources at 0 cannot be reduced further.

evidence.section: Assets, claiming, exhaustion and theft, discarded assets sentence
evidence.text: Gaining an asset puts it faceup in your play area. Winning a deal **claims** its revealed asset; trading, stealing or swapping merely gains it and does not trigger a “when you claim” ability. Discarded assets go facedown to the bottom of the asset deck.

answers.answer: Standard round phases are Action → Production → Event. In Production, exploit every android district in ascending district-number order; non-android districts are skipped. Reveal the top event and resolve top-to-bottom: upper effect, one copy of each listed component in every district beside that component, then the indicated next turn count. Place that many top assets facedown on turn slots starting at slot 1, one per slot; put the resolved event on the bottom of its deck and advance the round marker. No reset of the turn track is needed after the sixth standard round because there is no later Action Phase.

evidence.section: Standard round and active turn, phase-order sentence
evidence.text: A standard round has **Action → Production → Event** phases.

evidence.section: Production Phase, complete subsection
evidence.text:
Exploit every district containing an android, in ascending district-number order. A district without an android is not exploited in normal Production. Exploiting has two parts in order:

1. Produce its resources, applying the existing production modifiers below and increasing the matching supply tracks.
2. Increase its unrest by one stage, or two if it contains Human First. This still happens when it produced nothing. Apply the special Human First outage rule below.

Production does not trigger illness. After all android districts are exploited, proceed to Event.

evidence.section: Event Phase, complete subsection
evidence.text:
Reveal the top event and resolve it from top to bottom: its upper effect, then one copy of each listed component in every district beside that component, then the indicated next turn count. Place that many assets from the top of their deck facedown on the turn track, starting with slot 1, one per slot. The event's lower-right number is the turn count. Put the resolved event on the bottom of the event deck and advance the round marker.

Event backs warn of a relevant component; location and tier can affect the printed threat result. They are warnings, not a separate automatic threat rule: resolve the actual front's instructions. Components can spill along paths during placement and cause additional Root threat. Illness's action-triggered effect does not trigger from events. Melange checks the total threat increase during the entire event, including its placements. The turn track need not be reset after the sixth standard round because there is no subsequent Action Phase.

answers.answer: Liquidation produces a district’s resources without exploiting it: apply normal production modifiers, but not exploitation effects such as unrest increase. Caprice Nisei cannot affect Unorthodox Knowledge, and the player resolving Unorthodox Knowledge is not bound to resolve it in the way they announced.

evidence.section: FAQ & Rulings, complete relevant table rows
evidence.text:
| Card / interaction | Ruling |
|---|---|
| Liquidation | Produces a district's resources without exploiting it. Apply normal production modifiers, but do not apply normal exploitation effects such as unrest increase. |
| Unorthodox Knowledge / Caprice Nisei | Caprice cannot affect Unorthodox Knowledge. The player resolving Unorthodox Knowledge is not bound to resolve it in the way they stated. |

evidence.section: Production, unrest and outages, complete modifier table
evidence.text:
| Condition | Production / exploitation effect |
|---|---|
| Stable or protest | Can produce normally. |
| Strike | Produces no resources. Ordinary unrest increases cannot go beyond strike. |
| Outage | Produces no resources. Treat unrest as stable and unable to increase while the outage remains. |
| Development | Add 1 to the primary quantity only; never changes secondary. |
| Orgcrime | Produces no primary, even if developed. Secondary is still available. A one-resource district with orgcrime produces nothing. |
| Human First | Changes the unrest increase upon exploitation from 1 to 2 stages; does not itself prevent that exploitation's initial production. |
